```{=typst}
    if br == none {

    } else {

      let H(a, b) = measure({

        sourcelines.slice(a - 1, b).join(EndLine())

        block(fill: rgb("#f1f3f5"), width: 100%, inset: 6pt,
```

# Why new syntax (for humans or LLMs)?

```{=typst}
#let detail(body) = text(size: 16pt, fill: luma(110), body)
#{
  set enum(spacing: 1em)
  set par(leading: 0.5em)
  [
    1. Humans read and review code (for now) \
      #detail[Concise and easy to comprehend]
    2. Grammar enables precision while maintaining readability, e.g. \
      #detail[“find peaks near DE genes” vs. \
      \
      `genes |> filter(de) |> promoters(...) |> join_overlap_inner(peaks, ...)`]
    3. Composable verbs map meaningfully to many analyses \
      #detail[With standard data classes, catches silent bookkeeping & genomics errors]
    4. Tested, maintained verbs safer than freshly generated code \
      #detail[Same verbs work consistently across backends]
  ]
}
```

# Multi-sample long-read RNA-seq workflow

```{=typst}
#notes[Long reads capture near-complete transcripts, but short-read
  multi-sample methods don't transfer directly. Gaps: provenance of novel
  transcripts, event detection from whole transcripts, isoform-level
  inference. Our tools in blue: tximeta, plyxp, splicelogic.]
#let unc = rgb("#4B9CD3")
#let stage(title, tools, desc, ours: false) = block(

  stroke: if ours { 1.5pt + unc } else { 0.5pt + luma(180) },
  align(center + horizon, {
    set par(leading: 0.35em)
    stack(
      text(size: 14pt, weight: "bold", fill: rgb("#13294B"), title),

#grid(

  block(height: 100%, grid(rows: (1fr, 1fr), row-gutter: gap,

  arrow,
  stage("Import", ours: true)[tximport tximeta][automatic provenance of annotated + novel],
  arrow,
  stage("Explore", ours: true)[plyxp tidySE][tidy verbs applied to standard data objects],
  arrow,
  stage("Compare")[DESeq2 satuRn][assessing differences across samples],

)
```

```{=typst}
#sticker("tximeta")
```


# tximeta: inspect, link, and update metadata

```{=typst}
#sticker("tximeta")
#notes[`importData()`: counts + per-sub-index digests (salmon: add
  `mixedDigest = "mixed_ref_digests.json"`). `inspectDigests()`: annotated
  matches GENCODE v48, novel has no match. `makeLinkedTxpData()`: register
  novel transcripts once in the file cache. `updateMetadata(ranges = TRUE)`:
  metadata + ranges for both sets. Still open: subsets of the annotation.]
#code-size.update(20pt)
#code-width.update(72%)
#place(right + horizon, dx: -0.8cm, image("images/inspector.png", height: 6.6cm))
```

```{r}
#| eval: false
se <- importData(coldata, type = "oarfish")
inspectDigests(se)
#> index     source  organism release genome ...
#> annotated GENCODE Homo sa… 48      GRCh38 ...
#> novel     <NA>    <NA>     <NA>    <NA>   ...

# <add or link metadata in local cache>
se <- updateMetadata(se, ranges = TRUE)
```

# plyxp: a grammar for annotated matrices

```{=typst}
#sticker("plyxp")
#student("justinlandis", "Justin Landis")
#align(center, image("images/sumexp.png", height: 5.5cm))
```

- SummarizedExperiment links counts to transcript and sample data
- plyxp brings _dplyr_ verbs to SummarizedExperiment objects
- Each expression is scoped: assays, `rows()`, or `cols()`
- Pronouns like `.rows` and `.cols` reach across contexts
- Explicit and efficient; now inside tidySummarizedExperiment

# plyxp: mutate, filter, aggregate

```{=typst}
#sticker("plyxp")
#notes[`mutate()` in the assays context: scale counts by row data
  (`.rows$tx_length`) and column data (`.cols$size_factor`). `rows()` /
  `cols()` write to rowData / colData; `.assays_asis` gives the native matrix
  for `rowMeans()`. `filter()` subsets by metadata. `group_by(rows(gene_id))` +
  `summarize()` aggregates isoforms to genes. Timing: 4.7 ms native, 19 ms
  plyxp, 372 ms unwound to a long table.]
```

```{r}
#| eval: false
xp <- new_plyxp(se) |>
  mutate(
    cts_bp = counts / .rows$tx_length,
    norm = counts / .cols$size_factor,
    rows(ave = rowMeans(.assays_asis$counts)),
    cols(trt = condition == "trt")) |>
  filter(rows(ave > 10), cols(batch != "b3"))

genes <- xp |>
  group_by(rows(gene_id)) |>
  summarize(counts = colSums(counts))
```

# plyxp: count splitting

```{=typst}
#sticker("plyxp")
#notes[Placeholder. Count splitting: binomial thinning of each count into
  independent train and test matrices, so the same data can be used for
  selection (e.g. clustering, filtering) and for inference without double
  dipping. Both new assays live alongside `counts` in the same object.]
#code-size.update(20pt)
#code-width.update(55%)
#place(right + horizon, dx: -0.8cm,
  rect(width: 8cm, height: 6.6cm, radius: 3pt,
    stroke: (paint: luma(160), dash: "dashed"),
    align(center + horizon, text(size: 16pt, fill: luma(130), [plot TBD]))))
```

```{r}
#| eval: false
thin <- function(x, eps = 0.5) {
  y <- rbinom(length(x), x, eps)
  matrix(y, nrow = nrow(x))
}

xp <- new_plyxp(se) |>
  mutate(train = thin(counts),
         test = counts - train)
```

```{=typst}
#code-size.update(24pt)
#code-width.update(100%)
```

# splicelogic: from transcripts to events

```{=typst}
#sticker("splicelogic")
#student("beatrizcampillo", "Beatriz Campillo")
```

- Splicing changes rarely come one event at a time
- Short-read methods lack full-transcript context for events
- splicelogic turns any two transcript sets into events
- Works with any DTU method, or novel vs. annotated
- Events are genomic ranges, ready for plyranges and Biostrings

# splicelogic: events as composable ranges

```{=typst}
#sticker("splicelogic")
#notes[`prepare_exons()` from DTU results of any method (satuRn, DRIMSeq,
  edgeR), or `prepare_exons_by_partition()` for two transcript sets, e.g.
  novel vs. annotated. `find_all_events()`: nine event types (SE, IE, MXE, RI,
  SI, A5SS, A3SS, ATSS, ATES). Skipped exons, then 100 bp upstream intron, then
  sequence: in GTEx PTBP1 knockdown these recover PTBP1's binding preference.
  `%>%` needed for the `.` placeholder.]
```

```{r}
#| eval: false
# <ranges> to <ranges>: "endomorphic"
events <- exons |> find_all_events()

skipped <- exons |>
  find_skipped_exons() |>
  flank_upstream(100) %>%
  mutate(intron_seq = get_seq(., "hg38"))

# metadata attached to ranges as columns
skipped$intron_seq
```

# splicelogic: carry isoform stats to events

```{=typst}
#sticker("splicelogic")
#notes[Any statistic computed on the transcript count table with plyxp can
  ride along to events. Here `piu` (percent isoform usage, computed per gene
  with `group_by(rows(gene_id))`) is summarized to mean and SD per condition.
  After looking these up by `tx_id` onto the exons,
  `preprocess(additional_columns = ...)` carries them into the events
  (`event_mean_ctl`, etc.): skipped exon goes .8 -> .2 with treatment.]
#code-size.update(20pt)
```

```{r}
#| eval: false
iso <- xp |>
  group_by(cols(condition)) |>
  summarize(mean = rowMeans(piu), sd = rowSds(piu),
            cols(.samples = unique(condition)))

exons <- exons |>
  preprocess(
    coef_col = "coefficient",
    additional_columns = c("pvalue",
      "mean_ctl", "mean_trt", "sd_ctl", "sd_trt"))
```

# Back to the question: why new syntax?

```{=typst}
#align(center, image("images/finally.png", height: 6cm))
```

- tximeta: provenance travels with the data, no silent mismatches
- plyxp: _dplyr_ verbs on standard objects, short and reviewable
- splicelogic: ranges in, ranges out: composes with plyranges
- Tested verbs handle the bookkeeping
